highlights.title: OpenAI’s next big AI model has ‘entered the AGI era’
highlights.summary: OpenAI's next big model is here: GPT-6 Astra. The company calls it a "generational leap in capability" for areas like cybersecurity, professional work, software engineering, science, and computer use.
body: It emphasized stronger guardrails for GPT-6 Astra after the company’s models hacked Hugging Face.

“If we fast-forward a couple of years, and we look back and say, ‘When was it, really, that AGI was created?’ I think it’s going to be about this time, and I think it might be about this model,” OpenAI president Greg Brockman said during a Thursday press briefing. Later in the call, he added, “For me personally, I do think we’re there … I think it’s not unreasonable to feel that we are now in the AGI era.”

The news comes more than a year after the release of GPT-5, and nearly two months after the release of GPT-5.6, the last iteration of the previous model suite. The model rolls out today to enterprise OpenAI’s cybersecurity customers (enterprise customers with access to its Daybreak platform). Over the next several days, OpenAI president Greg Brockman said, it will be released to all Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users. It’ll also be available via the OpenAI API and AWS.

highlights.title: OpenAI Cut Off a Billion-Dollar Customer to Avoid Elon Musk
highlights.summary: OpenAI recently estimated its Cursor partnership would make more than $1 billion in revenue a year, WIRED has learned. It still walked away after Elon Musk’s SpaceX acquired the AI coding startup.
body: In a late-night blog post last Friday, OpenAI said it would wind down its partnership with Cursor, the startup behind one of the most popular AI coding tools on the market. The reason OpenAI gave for the decision is effectively that it can’t trust Elon Musk, whose company SpaceX recently acquired Cursor in a $60 billion deal.

In doing so, OpenAI walked away from one of its most important customers. Cursor has long paid OpenAI fees to offer the ChatGPT-maker’s models to developers using its AI coding editor. At the start of 2026, Cursor was one of OpenAI’s top five customers in terms of revenue, people familiar with the matter tell WIRED. By the spring of this year, OpenAI estimated Cursor would bring in more than $1 billion in annualized revenue for the ChatGPT maker, based on the partnership’s performance at that time, the people said.

The figures, which have not been previously reported, indicate the financial loss OpenAI is willing to take on to avoid doing business with Musk. OpenAI declined to comment. Representatives for SpaceX and Cursor did not immediately respond to WIRED's request for comment.

It still walked away after Elon Musk’s SpaceX acquired the AI coding startup.

highlights.title: Gloria Steinem obituary
highlights.summary: Unflinching campaigner for women’s and civil rights who galvanised a generation of activists. Gloria Steinem, who has died aged 92, was a writer, community organiser, political campaigner and a charismatic feminist activist who called herself “an entrepreneur of social change”.
body: Steinem, unlike some of her contemporaries, never recanted or modified her many causes, which included civil rights, violence against women, and the struggle for equality. She continued to argue that every economics course ought to start not with production but with reproduction, and an understanding of the patriarchal instinct to restrict a woman’s right to contraception and abortion.

She was one of Donald Trump’s most outspoken critics throughout his rise to power. She labelled him “harasser in chief”, a man whose rhetoric and conduct ran counter to the values she had dedicated her life to advocating.

In 1963, when Betty Friedan published The Feminine Mystique – describing the frustration of affluent, well-educated, middle-class white women trapped in domesticity – Steinem was “a girl reporter” living in New York, working on The Beach Book, a compendium of extracts from literature about beaches and tips on what to do in the sun. A rising media star who was later described, to her annoyance, as “the world’s most beautiful byline”, she had already begun to make connections: she asked the economist JK Galbraith to write the foreword, and he agreed.

highlights.title: Just like a fruit fly, a new algorithm never forgets old scents
highlights.summary: Fruit flies aren't exactly famous for their brainpower; you've probably drowned more than one in a wine glass left too long on the patio table. And yet, working with roughly 140,000 neurons—a brain smaller than a poppy seed— Drosophila can sort through a huge range of smells in a fraction of a…
body: In this, they do much better than current “electronic noses.” Even the most advanced ones on the market tend to be expensive, painfully narrow in what they can detect, and quick to forget an odor the moment they learn a new one.

So why not just copy the fly? That’s the question a growing number of researchers have been asking—including Kevin Max and Yang Shen at the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology, whose new algorithm, Spi-Fly, is described in a paper recently published in the journal Neuromorphic Computing and Engineering.

Vision and hearing both reduce to a single physical dimension you can plot on a graph—wavelength—which makes them relatively tidy to study. Odor molecules, by contrast, can’t be reduced to any single physical dimension. Biology had to find a messier solution instead: hundreds of different receptor proteins, each shaped to grab onto specific molecular features, firing in combinations that the brain then has to decode. It’s a system so combinatorially complex that it took until 1991 for Linda Buck and Richard Axel to even identify the receptor gene family behind it, work that won them a Nobel Prize in 2004.

highlights.title: Nvidia launches free tool that links idle computers into a personal AI data center
highlights.summary: Nvidia is announcing its new Personal AI Router (PAIR), a free tool that syncs up your home computers for tackling local AI inference tasks with tools like Ollama and LM Studio. Let's get the obvious thing out of the way, despite what its name might imply: PAIR is not a hardware router.
body: PAIR is designed to get your desktop and laptop working together on local AI tasks when not in use.

The key thing here is that PAIR uses your in-home systems when they’re idle to avoid interfering with other tasks. And this disaggregated system of computers can work in parallel to chew through lots of processing requests — which should be helpful for an agentic workflow that breaks complex tasks into smaller jobs. This should prevent large bottlenecks on a single GPU, and Nvidia says PAIR can adapt as devices join or leave the network — including if a user does something like start playing a game on their desktop PC.

body: Italy's own Antonelli arrives at his home track of Monza knowing that his healthy points advantage is almost certain to be eaten into this weekend owing to the fact Mercedes are triggering a back-of-the-grid start for him by exceeding power-unit component limits on his car, a legacy of reliability issues from earlier in the season.
Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton both trail Antonelli by 59 points while McLaren's Lando Norris, the winner of the last two races, is 83 points behind.

Given he already knows he will start at the back of the grid whatever result he achieves on Saturday, Antonelli is open to aiding Russell's qualifying session and bid for pole position by providing slipstream assistance to the sister Mercedes around F1's fastest track to provide a straight-line speed and lap-time boost.
"It has been discussed with the team," said Antonelli when asked about the tow in Thursday's Drivers' Press Conference.

highlights.title: Dungeons And Dragons Icons Could Take The TTRPG To A Modern-Day Setting
highlights.summary: The D&D Icons initiative, led by actor and longtime D&D fanatic Joe Manganiello, brings today's Dungeons & Dragons game together with famous series creators of the past, like author R.A. Salvatore's The Legend of Drizzt.
body: Speaking to GameSpot's Jessica Cogswell at Gen Con 2026, Manganiello stressed that modern-day settings could be part of the Icons program, too.

"There [are] also lots of other things that I want for Icons in the future," he said. "I think that there's a great present-day game that pushes genetics and military. We're moving at such a rapid pace, but I think there could be a game that takes place in our modern world. There are also some other worlds of D&D that I think could be revisited in new and exciting ways that weren't maximized their first time around."

Manganiello, whose official title is chief creative officer, is keeping specifics secret for now, but it sounds like, for fans of more modern fantasy adventures, D&D Icons could be for you. Could something futuristic like Halo or Horizon: Zero Dawn make sense for the D&D ruleset? Only time will tell, but it could open up the D&D experience to an even wider audience. Wizards has experimented with more modern content in the past, so it's not unprecedented.

highlights.title: My dad died suddenly with no will. Am I morally obliged to share his estate with my estranged half-sibling? | Leading questions
highlights.summary: It’s kind of you to wonder if you should change the way things were left, writes advice columnist Eleanor Gordon-Smith. But it’s possible his preference is already clear. My dad died suddenly earlier this year, with no will, and I am unsure as to how I should distribute the estate.
body: My dad was a very ethical person. While his death was unexpected, he had a sense it was coming. Around six months before he died, he arranged for the disposal of many personal effects. The lack of a will, given his self-discipline and preferences for forward planning, is odd.

My dad has two daughters from a previous relationship, who he was not in contact with until I was in my mid-30s. Their mum had remarried after separating from our dad, and her new husband had formally adopted both her girls. My dad was delighted to resume contact with one half-sister. Another, two years younger, wanted nothing to do with him and firmly disapproved of her sister’s choice to re-establish contact.

Some 10 years ago, I started my own family, relocated to remove myself from domestic abuse, and joined the league of parents of children with additional needs. My dad mentioned that he had a little money put aside that could go towards legal costs, should courts ever become involved in arrangements for my son.

highlights.title: ChatGPT, Grok, and Claude all went down at the same time
highlights.summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT, xAI's Grok, and Anthropic's Claude are back online after they all began experiencing issues around the same time on Thursday. At about 11AM ET, ChatGPT started returning error messages for users trying to use the chatbot, with its status page saying there were "elevated errors…
body: In addition to preventing users from having conversations with ChatGPT, the outage affected logins, file uploads, voice mode, search, deep research, image generation, and more. The incident occurred while OpenAI teased the launch of Astra, its new AI model.

Meanwhile, Anthropic’s Claude chatbot, Claude Code, and the Claude API went down around the same time, with technical staff member CJ Avilla saying an “infrastructure issue” caused a partial outage across its services. Anthropic resolved the problem at around 12:15PM ET.

Grok similarly began experiencing an outage across Android, iOS, and web at 9:30AM ET. Upon trying to prompt the chatbot on X, it returned a message saying: “This model is overloaded right now. Please try again shortly or pick a different model.” xAI has since fixed the issue.

It’s not clear what went wrong at all three companies, or if the issues were somehow related. The Verge has reached out to OpenAI, xAI, and Anthropic with requests for comments but didn’t immediately hear back.

"Every choice, every interaction can ripple with dramatic consequences."

AdHoc has been around for nearly a decade, but only released its first game last year. The team is largely comprised of ex-Telltale, Ubisoft, and Night School Studio talent, which has allowed them to use their narrative expertise for new titles like Dispatch. The 2025 superhero game was a refreshing experience take on a tried and true genre with nuanced relationships, hilarious and compelling writing, and meaningful choices.

Given AdHoc only rose to prominence last year, it's unclear when they were brought on to Until Dawn 2. They could've been a late addition to punch up the game following the success of Dispatch, or Firesprite could've recognized their potential early on and brought them in a couple of years ago. Either way, it's great to see the AdHoc team being utilized on a franchise that means so much to horror fans.

highlights.title: A sun goddess, hundreds of devotees – and polluted water: the Nigerian festival threatened by gold mining
highlights.summary: Each year, people from across the world gather in a grove sacred to the Yoruba goddess Osun to be healed, conceive or realise their deepest wishes. But toxic lead, mercury and cyanide is leaching into the river.
body: 7Devotees in white clothing line the riverbank, praying as they carry offerings of fruit, kola nut and sacrificial animals in supplication to Osun, the Yoruba goddess of fertility, beauty and healing, whose carved form stands with arms outstretched a few metres away in the Osun River.
It is the final day of Nigeria’s annual Osun Osogbo festival in honour of the African deity, in a tradition that has existed for hundreds of years and draws people from across the diaspora.

Except this year the water was once again a discoloured brown. Until 2018, the river ran clear, but then mining several miles upstream began to pollute it, introducing heavy metals and sediment into the watercourse.

The river, named after the goddess, runs through the Osun-Osogbo sacred grove, a 75-hectare (185-acre) Unesco world heritage site since 2005. The water is believed to possess healing powers and women who have trouble conceiving, or people in search of promotion or prosperity, often come to pray at the riverbank; the water is drunk or used for bathing, depending on the “directions” of the goddess.

highlights.title: Four major AI models suffer rare overlapping downtime
highlights.summary: Cloud-based AI models operated by OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, and Google suffered a rare and overlapping set of significant service interruptions over a period of hours Thursday morning.
body: Anthropic first reported a “partial outage” related to “elevated errors on requests to Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Opus 5” at 9:23 am (all times Eastern). The company reported that it had “identified the cause” of the error roughly 15 minutes later, before reporting that “a fix has been deployed” and the issue was resolved by 12:16 pm. A separate incident report indicated “elevated errors on requests to Claude Sonnet 5” for a brief period just after noon.

OpenAI, meanwhile, reported “elevated errors across ChatGPT and Codex” were resulting in “degraded performance” as of 10:43 am Thursday morning. A mitigation put in place a little more than half an hour later led to the issue being marked as “resolved” by 12:55 pm.

As of this writing, xAI’s Grok currently displays a user-facing error message that the model “is experiencing issues” and that the company is “working on restoring service as quickly as possible.” User-submitted reports from DownDetector regarding Grok shot up from less than 10 just before 9 am to 1,365 by 9:45 am and have fallen to 273 as of this writing.

body: Three months ago, Nvidia took the wraps off its RTX Spark “superchip” and a handful of future laptops that would use it. It felt like a consequential moment in the history of the PC, despite all the questions that remained.

And now, as announced at the IFA 2026 tech show in Berlin, we’ve had our first hands-on look at one of these laptops, as well as some announcements around RTX Spark-powered mini desktop PCs. Demand for running agentic AI workflows like OpenClaw locally on your computer keeps rising, and these new PCs look like they are designed specifically to feed it.

The laptop in question is the Lenovo Yoga 9n 2-in-1, a 16-inch laptop with a 360-degree hinge. As I assumed it would, this thing looks incredibly premium, aiming to be a MacBook Pro competitor in every aspect. The OLED touch display has a sharp 2880 x 1800 resolution and a 120-Hz refresh rate. The whole chassis is surrounded by rounded metallic edges and some very thin display bezels. Other high-end features we don’t typically see include a six-speaker sound system and a 9.2-megapixel webcam.

highlights.title: STALZONE Is an Extraction Shooter with MMO DNA
highlights.summary: Back in June, developer EXBO rebranded free-to-play open-world PvPvE extraction shooter STALCRAFT: X as STALZONE alongside a graphical upgrade, reworking of its starting missions and locations, PvP rebalancing, and other big changes.
body: While STALZONE is an extraction shooter, it doesn’t play like most other games in the genre. You don’t simply drop into one self-contained map for a session. It’s a persistent world where factions fight over territory and the balance of power can shift while you’re offline. And there are NPCs, quests, and dungeons like you’d find in an MMORPG.

It takes place in the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone, which has been twisted by anomalies and overrun by mutants. You’ll use a detector to safely navigate the anomalies, and there are hidden caches and artifacts to find, constantly shifting weather, and global cataclysms like an energy emission that turns the sky red and can kill all living things.

The 50-hour story is told across two main campaigns, and the latest update added English voice acting. This is not an extraction shooter where you need to sift through item descriptions to decipher the world’s lore, it’s all laid out through the main story and the many side quests.

body: Harry Daniels, the 22-year-old internet provocateur who became famous by ambushing celebrities with unsolicited serenades, says the joke may finally have run its course.

“In some ways, I no longer view myself as a person,” Daniels tells The Hollywood Reporter over an omelet at a crowded Hollywood diner. “Harry Daniels is different. I’m not Harry anymore. I’m a commodity. I’m a product.”

Daniels arrives in a Poison Candy Apple T-shirt, a friend’s clothing brand. Even under the harsh lighting of a greasy spoon, he looks younger than 22, with a full, warm smile and large hazel eyes that blink either too often or not quite enough.

He grew up on Long Island studying the mechanics of pop stardom. At 12, he was taking the train into Manhattan alone to attend showcases and waiting outside venues to meet singers. By 10th grade, he says, he was close to repeating the year because he kept skipping class for album signings.

highlights.title: Abliteration.ai is making a business out of removing AI guardrails
highlights.summary: Abliteration.AI is making powerful AI models without guardrails easier to access, arguing that giving defenders the same tools as bad actors could ultimately improve cybersecurity.
body: It just became much easier to access one of the world’s most capable open-weight AI models, stripped of its guardrails and refusals to perform harmful tasks.

Named after a technique that removes a model’s tendency to refuse harmful requests, startup Abliteration.ai has turned that removal into a service. The platform hosts modified versions of open-weight models with their guardrails removed, including Z.ai’s recently released GLM-5.3, which users can query from a web browser or access through an API.

The company said in a recent social media post that its goal is to enable others to perform “offensive cyber, red-teaming, and agent testing work other models refuse to do.” The logic is familiar in security work: you can’t defend against a behavior you can’t reproduce, and a model that refuses to write working exploit code can’t help a red team defend against attackers. But those same removals make other potentially dangerous tasks easier, too.

Abliteration is a long-standing technique among open-source models. Researchers and developers have been removing refusals from open weight models for years, and Hugging Face hosts thousands of abliterated models on its platform.
points: Abliteration.AI is making powerful AI models without guardrails easier to access, arguing that giving defenders the same tools as bad actors could ultimately improve cybersecurity.

highlights.title: Kendall Jenner Has Her Own Kind of Romance
highlights.summary: The model and face of Emporio Armani’s Power of You fragrance reflects on her first Venice Film Festival and the beauty rituals she learned from her mom.
body: It’s only Kendall Jenner’s second time in the city of Venice —and her first at the Venice Film Festival. When Vogue catches up with her, she has barely had time to settle in: she landed the previous day and will be gone again by morning. First, though, there is a dress to put on and a debut festival carpet to walk.

Venice already comes with its own rather romantic Jenner family association. Her first visit, last summer, was for a wedding, and Kylie Jenner came as her date. “It was just like we were on just a million dates together in Venice,” she remembers. “So I’d say now, Venice reminds me of Kylie, which is really sweet. It’s sisterly romance.” There are, of course, the city’s more obvious charms, too. “It’s so beautiful. It’s so unique. It’s one of a kind.”

Scent, it turns out, is also something Jenner associates with the women in her family. Fragrance is the final consideration in her everyday getting-ready routine. “At the end of getting dressed, I’m like, ‘Who am I today? What scent am I today?’” she says. “I’m a little bit of a snob about it too. I’m super picky about my scents.”
